facts.raw_span: 61-year-old woman with type II diabetes
several days of urinary retention
1-year history of progressive lower-extremity weakness
100-lb unintentional weight loss
bilateral weakness of hip flexors, knee flexors, knee extensors, and intrinsic hand muscles
atrophy of the hands and thighs
sensation to light touch was reduced in the feet
reflexes were 2+ in the upper extremities and absent at the knees and ankles
bladder catheterization yielded 1.8 L of retained urine
CSF analysis revealed protein 175 mg/dL
electromyography and nerve conduction studies demonstrated decreased amplitudes in motor and sensory nerves
MRI of the pelvis showed bilateral femoral nerve enlargement without enhancement

concepts.why: The patient's progressive lower-extremity weakness, bilateral weakness of hip flexors and knee extensors, and reduced sensation to light touch in the feet are consistent with a chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy.
The patient's type II diabetes, progressive lower-extremity weakness, and bilateral femoral nerve enlargement on MRI are consistent with diabetic amyotrophy.
The patient's urinary retention and significant post-void residual volume are consistent with a neuropathic bladder due to underlying polyneuropathy.

The patient's bilateral weakness of hip flexors and knee extensors, atrophy of the hands and thighs, and bilateral femoral nerve enlargement on MRI are consistent with a chronic lumbosacral plexopathy.
It explains the absent reflexes and elevated CSF protein levels.

rationales.F02: Urinary retention is a common symptom of polyneuropathy.
rationales.F03: Progressive lower-extremity weakness is a characteristic symptom of chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy and chronic lumbosacral plexopathy.
rationales.F05: Bilateral weakness of hip flexors, knee flexors, knee extensors, and intrinsic hand muscles is consistent with chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy and chronic lumbosacral plexopathy.
rationales.F08: Absent reflexes at the knees and ankles are consistent with chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy.
rationales.F11: Electromyography and nerve conduction studies demonstrating decreased amplitudes in motor and sensory nerves are consistent with chronic length-dependent sensorimotor demyelinating polyneuropathy.
